Relatively safer day Relatively safer night

In detail

Northumbria Police recorded 188 crimes inside this ward's official boundary over the 3 months to July 2026 — 6.5 per 1,000 residents, the 20th highest rate of Newcastle upon Tyne's 26 wards. The daytime score here is driven by shoplifting (24), burglary (2), vehicle crime (2); the evening/night score by violent crime (12), anti social behaviour (7), public order (4). Rated against the average of the city's own wards, never against another city.

Frequently asked questions

Is Dene & South Gosforth safe?

Wandroz currently rates Dene & South Gosforth in Newcastle upon Tyne as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Newcastle upon Tyne during the day and relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Newcastle upon Tyne at night. This rating is derived from Northumbria Police street-level crime records published at data.police.uk — an official statistic, not an assessment. High-footfall tourist, transit or shopping areas can read higher on this kind of measure without that meaning elevated risk per visit, since these statistics are normalised against registered residents rather than footfall — see the note on this page and the methodology page for the full caveats.

Is Dene & South Gosforth safe at night?

At night, Dene & South Gosforth is rated as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Newcastle upon Tyne. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Dene & South Gosforth a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Dene & South Gosforth's day rating (relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Newcastle upon Tyne) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
